findings.fix: Use the hom API: `(hcomm.map (points r K).subtype).map (Units.coeHom _)`, or follow the existing idiom (congrArg at GL level, then `rw [Subgroup.coe_mul, Units.val_mul]`).
findings.issue: `have hmatrix : Commute d.1.1 g.1.1 := congrArg (fun x : points r K ↦ x.1.1) hcomm.eq` type-checks only by unfolding `Commute`/`SemiconjBy` and the componentwise `mul` of both the `Subgroup` subtype and `Units`; no comment documents this.

findings.evidence: Lines 184-189 produce `hcomm : Commute (↑(weightTorusPoints r K s)) g` in `GL (Fin (r+1)) K` while the goal is `Commute (weightTorusPoints r K s) g` in the subgroup.
findings.issue: `apply Subtype.ext; exact hcomm.eq` closes a `Commute` goal in `points r K` from a `Commute` at GL level: `Subtype.ext` is applied to a goal that is only definitionally an equation, and `↑(d * g) = ↑d * ↑g` is used silently. Same undocumented-defeq class as line 164 (and, more mildly, the closing `rfl` of `mem_diagonalPoints_iff` at line 141).

findings.evidence: Mathlib has `partialProd_zero/succ/succ'/init/left_inv/right_inv/contractNth` (mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Fin.lean:487-569) but no `partialProd_last`; grep for `partialProd` in ./code shows this file is the only user.
findings.fix: Factor a lemma `partialProd_last (f : Fin n → M) : Fin.partialProd f (Fin.last n) = ∏ i, f i`, proved from `Fin.partialProd_succ`/induction, and use it here.
findings.issue: `hlast` proves the general fact `Fin.partialProd t (Fin.last n) = ∏ i, t i` inline by unfolding the definition (`rw [Fin.partialProd, Fin.val_last]`) and doing `List.take`/`List.ofFn` surgery, hiding a reusable lemma inside one branch of a private proof.

findings.evidence: Lines 62, 76, 94, 95, 111 of the new file; each `simp` is followed by further tactics or by a `Fin.ext` obligation depending on the exact simp normal form of `(⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin r).succ.castSucc`.
findings.fix: Replace with `simp only [Fin.val_succ, Fin.val_castSucc, ...]` (or `dsimp only`) followed by `omega`, so the goal handed to `omega` is fixed.
findings.issue: Index equalities are closed by a default `simp` whose output is handed to `omega`: `Fin.ext (by simp [c])` (62), `Fin.ext (by simp [c]; omega)` (76), `Fin.ext (by simp [i])` (94), `Fin.ext (by simp [j]; omega)` (95), `Fin.ext (by simp [i, k]; omega)` (111). Non-terminal `simp` with the full simp set makes these break on any change to `Fin` normal forms.

findings.evidence: Lines 91-128: branches are distinguished only by `have hkzero : (k : ℕ) = 0 := by omega`, `have hkmax : (k : ℕ) = r := by omega`, `have hrzero : r = 0 := by omega`.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment at the head of each `·` branch naming the case it handles.
findings.issue: `torusCharacter_partialProd` is a 40-line four-way `split_ifs with hkr hk0` whose branches (interior `0 < k < r`, `k = 0`, `k = r`, degenerate `r = 0`) are nowhere named; the reader must reconstruct the case split from the `omega` calls.

summary: Two Commute conversions are typed through Subgroup and Units wrappers by raw definitional unfolding rather than the coercion lemmas the repo already uses elsewhere, a reusable `partialProd (Fin.last _)` fact is inlined by unfolding `Fin.partialProd`'s definition and doing List.take surgery, and several index equalities are closed by non-terminal default `simp` feeding `omega`.
